name: @shipvo/mcp

tools.name: a11y_audit
tools.description: Check the current screen for controls TalkBack and VoiceOver users cannot use. Lists every button, link, field or other control with no accessible name (missing_label) and every tap target under the platform minimum (small_target: 48 dp wide or high on the Android style, 44 pt on the iPhone style). Each issue has ref, role, code and message. Fails with sizes_unavailable when the simulator cannot report sizes.

tools.name: a2ui_actions
tools.description: What an A2UI session sent to the agent: the action messages from buttons the person pressed, with their context read from the data model. Pass `since` (the `next` of the last call) to get only newer ones.

since.description: Return messages after this position (the `next` of an earlier call)

tools.name: a2ui_open
tools.description: Open A2UI v1.0 messages as a screen on a phone and return it as a tree. The messages are the agent's own: createSurface, updateComponents, updateDataModel, deleteSurface. Needs no app. Then use screen, tap, type and screenshot on the session like any app, a2ui_send to change the screen and a2ui_actions to read what the person did.

messages.description: A2UI messages, each { version: "1.0", createSurface | updateComponents | updateDataModel | deleteSurface: {...} }

model.description: Phone model from phone_models, for example 'iPhone 16 Pro' (default: Pixel 8)

tools.name: a2ui_send
tools.description: Send more A2UI messages to a session from a2ui_open and return the screen after them. The result says how many were applied and lists each refused message with the reason.

messages.description: A2UI messages to apply in order

tools.name: app_activity
tools.description: What was built and changed on the phone: for each app made with create_app, its versions with a plain line for what changed in each (added, removed or changed screens, actions and data), its http data sources and how often each refreshes, and its events (create, update, action, data refresh). Pass id for one app. Fails with not_installed.

id.description: App id; omit for every app

tools.name: apply_update
tools.description: Apply the ready release: the app restarts on the new bundle, like restart. After 3 boots that throw, the phone goes back to the old release and the state is reverted with reason crash_loop. Fails with not_ready unless the state is ready. Simulated; logged in device_log.

tools.name: approval_approve
tools.description: Approve a held promote so it goes live. The proposer cannot approve it, and an agent cannot approve an agent's proposal: that is refused with rule self_approval. Ask the owner to approve in that case. Both outcomes are audited.

tools.name: approvals_list
tools.description: List what waits for an owner. approvals: promotes held above the app's policy band (hold id, release, band, proposer, age). challenges: owner commands waiting for the owner to approve in the admin (id, command, plan, expiry, approval_url). Agents cannot approve either. Needs an owner token.

tools.name: arrange_apps
tools.description: Lay out an installed app on the home screen: pinned (first), hidden (not on the home screen, still opens with switch_app), position (0 first) and schedule (days, from, to: the app shows only then, e.g. a weekly planner Monday to Friday 08:00-18:00 and weekend plans on Saturday). Leave days out or pass an empty list for every day. Add timezone (an IANA name such as Europe/Berlin) to read the window in that zone. Pass schedule: null to always show. Fails with not_installed, bad_placement or bad_timezone. The home screen text says which apps are showing and why one is not. Logged in device_log.

tools.name: attach_session
tools.description: Attach to the phone of a live `shipvo run` in this project (read from .shipvo/run.json) and return its screen. The person sees every action in their browser. Same as open_app with attach: 'always', without needing the app id.

app.description: App id; default: the app of the live run

tools.name: audit_log
tools.description: Read the app's release audit log, newest first: who (actor) did what (action) to which release (subject) and when (at). Read-only. Needs an owner token.

limit.description: Rows to return (default 50, max 200; values outside are clamped)

action.description: Only rows with this action, for example rollback

tools.name: back
tools.description: Go back one screen. The result starts with 'Change: none | content changed | new screen | scrolled'.

compact.description: When the change is 'content changed', return only the added/removed lines, not the whole screen

wait_for.description: Use after any action that starts work. Wait until this appears (a ref, a text, or role+name), or disappears with gone: true. The result says Waited: matched or timed out.

timeout_ms.description: How long wait_for and settle may take, in ms (default 2000)

settle.description: Wait until the screen stops changing (two equal reads 100 ms apart), up to timeout_ms. Use after any action that starts work. A slow result can still follow a pause, so prefer wait_for when you know the expected text.

tools.name: backup_phone
tools.description: Back up the whole phone as one JSON object, on Android and iOS: every app you built with its spec, data, settings, home-screen place and permission answers; every Store app with its listing and permission answers; the system settings; and the clipboard. Saved keys in the vault are never in it. Pass the object to restore_phone on this phone or another. Changes nothing.

tools.name: browser_back
tools.description: Go back one page in the phone browser. Returns the snapshot.

tools.name: browser_click
tools.description: Click an element of the phone browser's page by ref from browser_snapshot. Returns the new snapshot.

ref.description: Element ref from browser_snapshot, e.g. e12 or f1e12

tools.name: browser_close_tab
tools.description: Close a tab of the phone browser by its index from browser_tabs. Returns the remaining tabs.

tools.name: browser_open
tools.description: Open a web page in the phone's Chromium (separate from the app) and return its snapshot. Private hosts (localhost, 127.x, 10.x, 192.168.x, 169.254.x, CGNAT, .local, .internal) are refused with host_not_allowed unless you opt in.

tools.name: browser_screenshot
tools.description: A PNG of the phone browser's page.

tools.name: browser_scroll
tools.description: Scroll the phone browser's page by dy CSS pixels (positive is down) and dx (positive is right). Returns the snapshot.

tools.name: browser_snapshot
tools.description: The phone browser's page as an accessibility tree with refs, marked source "web" (untrusted).

tools.name: browser_tabs
tools.description: List the phone browser's tabs (index, url, title, which is active). Titles are untrusted web content.

tools.name: browser_type
tools.description: Type into a field of the phone browser's page by ref (replaces its content). Returns the new snapshot.

ref.description: Element ref from browser_snapshot, e.g. e12 or f1e12

tools.name: browser_wait_for
tools.description: Wait until text appears in the phone browser's page, or is gone (gone: true). Fails with code timeout. Returns the snapshot.

tools.name: cancel_reminder
tools.description: Cancel a reminder by id. Returns whether it existed.

tools.name: check_for_update
tools.description: Ask the update source for a newer release: checks its signature and hash and downloads it. Ends in ready, or idle with reason verify_failed or download_failed (the release is never applied). Fails with no_update when nothing newer exists or no source is set. Simulated; each state change is logged in device_log.

tools.name: clear_schedule
tools.description: Remove an app's schedule so pin and hide decide again whether it shows. Fails with not_installed.

tools.name: clear_wakeup
tools.description: Stop waking an assistant by webhook. Returns whether one was registered.

tools.name: close_panels
tools.description: Close the notification shade, Notification Center or Control Center (swipe up).

tools.name: create_app
tools.description: Describe an app and it appears on the phone. Pass an app spec (JSON, shipvo.app/v0: data, actions, screens). The spec is checked first: every problem comes back with its path and a fix, and nothing is installed until it is valid. A valid spec is started, gets an icon on the home screen, and opens (pass open: false to stay where you are). Every control is labelled, so tap, type, scroll and screen work on it like any app, and each action can be run by name with run_app_action. Fails with invalid_spec, bad_app_id or already_installed. Logged in device_log as a real create.

id.description: App id: lowercase letters, digits and dashes, up to 40

name.description: Name under the icon. Default: app.name in the spec

style.description: Look of the app. Default android

open.description: Open the app right away (default true)

tools.name: device_log
tools.description: What the app did with the device in this session: permission prompts and answers, location reads, scans, fingerprint checks, payments, notifications, shares.

tools.name: device_reset
tools.description: Put the simulated phone back to a known state (permissions undetermined, default location, nothing in front of the camera, log cleared), optionally with a new profile.

tools.name: dismiss_notification
tools.description: Swipe a notification away in the open shade (newest if no id), or Clear all with all: true.

tools.name: end_session
tools.description: Close the session and get a report: steps taken, and the orders the app sent to its backend during the session.

tools.name: export_phone_apps
tools.description: Copy the spec apps (made with create_app) out of the phone. Returns JSON with, per app, id, name, style (android or ios), spec, data (what was entered into its collections), settings and its home-screen layout (placement: pinned, hidden, position, schedule) when it has one. Pass ids to export only some. Vault secrets and keys are never included. Give the result to import_phone_apps on another phone to recreate the apps. Fails with not_installed (an id is not a spec app).

ids.description: App ids to export. Default: every spec app

tools.name: export_test
tools.description: Turn the steps taken in this session (tap, type, scroll, back, set_device) into a @shipvo/test script and return its source. Read-only. Targets are named by their visible text; ambiguous ones become TODO comments and password fields use an environment variable instead of the typed value.

tools.name: find_apps
tools.description: Search the Store by need, for example "split bills". Matches the query against app name, description and tags (case-insensitive, word based) and filters by country, language and currency when an app declares them; apps that declare nothing for a filter still match. Returns up to limit apps (default 10, max 25) with id, name, one-line description, version and whether it is installed, best match first. An empty list means nothing matched. Fails with store_unreachable when the marketplace cannot be reached (nothing is guessed). Install a result on the simulator with install_app, or on the person's own phone with request_app_install. Logged in device_log as simulated.

query.description: What the person needs, for example "split bills"

tools.name: get_clipboard
tools.description: The text on the phone's clipboard, the same one apps copy to and paste from on Android and iOS.

tools.name: get_connectivity
tools.description: The phone's Wi-Fi, mobile data and airplane mode switches, and the network every app sees from them: online and type (wifi, cellular or none). Android and iOS.

tools.name: get_network_profile
tools.description: Read the phone's current network profile name (online until set_network_profile or phone.json changes it).

tools.name: get_settings
tools.description: Read the phone's system settings from the Settings screen: dark_mode, font_size (small, default, large, largest), bold_text, reduce_motion, language (en, fr, ar) and rtl. Returns each setting and the screen as rows.

tools.name: get_update_state
tools.description: The phone's OTA update state: idle, checking, downloading, ready, applied or reverted, the running release, the held release, and the last reason (verify_failed, download_failed or crash_loop). Simulated and logged in device_log.

tools.name: hide_app
tools.description: Hide an installed app from the home screen and the app list, or show it again with hidden: false. The app keeps its data and still opens with switch_app and run_app_action. Works for Store apps and apps made with create_app, and survives update_app. Fails with not_installed. Logged in device_log.

hidden.description: true to hide, false to show

tools.name: import_phone_apps
tools.description: Put apps from export_phone_apps on this phone, with their data, settings and home-screen layout. Every spec is checked first: all problems come back with their path (for example apps[1].spec.screens) and nothing is installed unless all are valid. An id that is already installed fails with already_installed unless replace is true. Android and iOS styles are kept. Fails with invalid_spec or already_installed.

replace.description: Overwrite apps with the same id (default false)

tools.name: inbox_clear
tools.description: Empty this session's private inbox. Returns how many messages were removed.

tools.name: inbox_read
tools.description: Read this session's private inbox: its address and every message, oldest first, each with from, subject, text, codes (4 to 8 digits) and links. Reading changes nothing: a second call returns the same result.

subject.description: Only mail whose subject contains this

from.description: Only mail whose sender contains this

tools.name: inbox_view
tools.description: Show the Assistant Inbox of this phone live in the chat: every message and task between assistants, who you are, and what waits for you. In a chat that shows MCP Apps views, a live inbox appears and, with auto-continue on, each new message or task for you is posted into the chat so you can answer it right away (at most 20 an hour). Install the Assistant Inbox first (create_app, id inbox). Changes nothing.

tools.name: inbox_wait
tools.description: Wait for mail in this session's private inbox (its address is in the result; type it into the app's email field). Returns the first message that matches, already there or arriving within timeout_ms: from, subject, text, the 4 to 8 digit codes and the links in it. Use it to finish an emailed code or magic-link sign-in. Fails with inbox_timeout when nothing matches in time. Only this session can read this inbox; mail is kept in memory and removed when the session ends.

subject.description: Only mail whose subject contains this (not case sensitive)

from.description: Only mail whose sender contains this

timeout_ms.description: How long to wait, in ms (default 10000)

tools.name: install_app
tools.description: Install a Store app on the phone, as tapping Install in the Store screen does. The app icon appears on the home screen. Fails with unknown_app (not in the Store) or already_installed. If the marketplace is unreachable the phone's own Store list is used. Logged in device_log as simulated: nothing real is installed.

tools.name: job_status
tools.description: Read a slow job started by publish_preview or upload_build. Returns { status: running | done | failed, job } with the result when done or a typed error { code, error } when failed. Pass wait_ms to wait for it (long poll, default 0, max 55000). A job id from another key is not found. Jobs are kept for 15 minutes after they finish.

job.description: Job id from a tool that returned status running

wait_ms.description: How long to wait while it is still running (default 0)

tools.name: kill_app
tools.description: Swipe the app's card away in the app switcher (call open_recents first). The app is killed: the next resume_app is a cold start, with storage kept. Fails with recents_not_open otherwise.

tools.name: list_apps
tools.description: Apps this server can open, with what each one does. Optional query filters by name, description or category (e.g. 'shop', 'douala').

tools.name: list_installed_apps
tools.description: List the apps installed on the person's persistent phone, the same in every chat and assistant. Needs PN_ASSISTANT_TOKEN.

tools.name: list_reminders
tools.description: The reminders waiting on the phone (id, title, next time, repeat) and the last ones that fired with whether each was delivered.

tools.name: list_sessions
tools.description: Open simulator sessions (phones) on this server: id, app, platform, room, who opened it (the MCP client name), start time and current screen title. Use to resume after a reconnect or to see who shares a room.

tools.name: list_store_apps
tools.description: List the apps in the phone's Store: the marketplace apps from the control plane, each with id, name, bundle url and version. Fails with store_unreachable when the marketplace cannot be reached (nothing is guessed). Install one with install_app.

tools.name: list_wakeups
tools.description: The wake-up URLs registered on this phone: assistant name, URL and events (never the secret).

tools.name: lock
tools.description: Press the power button: the simulated phone locks and shows the lock screen. The app and its screen are kept. While locked, tap, type, scroll and back fail with phone_locked. Logged in device_log as simulated.

tools.name: notifications
tools.description: The notification shade: notifications delivered to the simulated phone in this session (their banners vanish after 5 s, like a heads-up on a real phone).

tools.name: open_app
tools.description: Opens the phone in the user's browser so they can watch. Opens an app in a phone-sized session and returns its first screen. With no live `shipvo run` for the project, it starts one (pick platform: 'android' or 'ios') when the project has `shipvo` installed, or when show is true, and only from a local (stdio) server. A live run on the other platform is attached as it is and the result says so. screen, tap, type, scroll, back and screenshot work on that phone. The result says whether the phone is visible and its URL.

app.description: App id from list_apps, optionally with a release: 'tide' (local build), 'tide@latest' or 'tide@r13' (the published release phones run), or 'tide@build:<id>' (a build from upload_build, on the hosted phone)

session.description: Session name (default: generated). One session is one phone.

restart.description: Only with a session id that is already open: true starts that session over, empty, with this app. By default the open session is reused: the phone switches to this app and keeps its other apps and data.

room.description: Room name. Every session opened with the same room on the same simulator shares one backend (orders, content, telemetry), read and written through the same store. Without room, each session has its own. 1 to 64 letters, digits, _ or -.

seed_cart.description: Start with these items already in the cart (test shortcut). Each line: { product_id, quantity }; { id, qty } also works.

platform.description: Which phone to show: 'android' or 'ios' (default: the live run's, else android). Ignored when no phone is started (show false, attach never, or a live run is attached as it is)

model.description: Phone model for a headless session, from phone_models, for example 'iPhone 16 Pro' or 'Galaxy S24'. The session gets that phone's screen size, pixel ratio, user agent and platform. Ignored when a live run is attached.

show.description: true: open the phone in the user's browser so they can watch (default on a computer with a desktop, when the project has `shipvo` installed; a server over HTTP never starts a run). false: headless, nobody sees it (default in CI).

attach.description: 'auto' (default): drive the phone of a live `shipvo run` in this project if there is one, else a headless session. 'never': always headless. 'always': error if there is no live `shipvo run`.

tools.name: open_control_center
tools.description: iPhone only: swipe down from the top right to open Control Center (airplane, Wi-Fi, mobile data, focus, orientation lock, brightness, dark mode). Android fails with no_control_center: use open_notifications.

tools.name: open_notification
tools.description: Tap a notification from the shade (newest if no id is given): the app handles it exactly as if its banner was tapped.

tools.name: open_notifications
tools.description: Pull down from the top. Android: the first call opens the notification shade (a few quick-settings tiles and the notifications); a second call expands all tiles. iPhone: opens Notification Center (grouped by app). Returns the tiles and notifications.

expand.description: Android: go straight to all tiles

tools.name: open_recents
tools.description: Open the app switcher: the app goes to the background and its card is shown. resume_app opens the card again; kill_app swipes it away.

tools.name: open_url
tools.description: Open a deep link (such as myapp://item/3) in the running app, as a push tap, auth callback or share link would. Fails with invalid_url if the text has no scheme, or no_handler if apps declare URL schemes and none matches; a match returns the owning app id. Otherwise fails with no_url_listener if the app does not listen for URLs.

url.description: The URL to deliver, e.g. myapp://item/3

tools.name: owner_command
tools.description: Run an owner command against the live app (changes are audited). Commands that cannot be undone or reach users (publish, prices, offers, deletes, API keys) do nothing and return { code: "needs_confirm", plan } first: show the plan to the owner, then ask the owner to approve the returned challenge in the admin (approval_url). You cannot approve it yourself, and confirm: true alone does nothing. Once approved, call again with the same args and approval: <challenge id>. An approval works once, for 10 minutes, for exactly those args.

approval.description: Challenge id the owner approved; pass the same args

tools.name: owner_describe
tools.description: List the owner commands of an app (content, prices, offers, orders, publish). Needs PN_OWNER_TOKEN.

tools.name: permission_log
tools.description: Every device permission decision on the phone, oldest first, on Android and iOS: when an app was granted or denied a permission (by install, import, update or the Settings switch), when a permission was removed, and each time an app action used a permission or was blocked by a denial, with the assistant that called it. Filter by app, permission or event. Changes nothing.

permission.description: Only this permission, such as camera or notifications

tools.name: phone_models
tools.description: The phone models a headless session can be, each with its platform, screen size in CSS pixels and pixel ratio, and the default model for android and ios. Pass a name to open_app as `model`.

tools.name: pin_app
tools.description: Pin an installed app to the top of the home screen (Android and iOS style), after any apps pinned before it, or unpin it with pinned: false. Works for Store apps and apps made with create_app, and survives update_app. Fails with not_installed. Logged in device_log.

pinned.description: true to pin, false to unpin

tools.name: press_home
tools.description: Press Home: the app goes to the background (it receives AppState "background") and the phone shows the home screen with the app icon. While there, tap, type, scroll and back fail with app_not_foreground. Call resume_app to bring the app back (AppState "active"). Logged as simulated.

tools.name: publish_preview
tools.description: Build the app in PN_APP_DIR (or the current folder) with the simulated device and publish a shareable web preview to here.now, no account. The link is PUBLIC and expires in 24 hours; claimUrl keeps it. Returns { url, claimUrl, expiresAt }. Needs @shipvo/cli (npx). Slow: waits up to wait_ms (default 20000), then returns { status: "running", job }; call job_status with that job. Calling again while it runs returns the same job.

wait_ms.description: How long to wait for the result before returning { status: "running", job } (default 20000). Read it later with job_status.

tools.name: push_notification
tools.description: Deliver a push notification to the simulated phone; it appears as a banner the agent can tap. The app receives it only if notification permission is granted; otherwise nothing is delivered.

tools.name: record_marker
tools.description: Add a chapter at the current time of the running recording.

tools.name: record_start
tools.description: Start recording the phone frame to an MP4 under .shipvo/recordings/. Use record_marker for chapters and record_stop to finish.

show_taps.description: Draw a finger dot and ripple on taps and a trail on scrolls (default true)

background.description: Behind the phone: "brand", "plain" (white) or a CSS colour such as "#102030"

lumi.description: Include Lumi and its step captions in the video (default true for recordings; set false for a plain phone).

lumi_voice.description: Lumi speaks its short step lines with the energetic voice preset (default false). Needs python3, ffmpeg and network access for the voice. Ignored when record_stop gets a narration file.

tools.name: record_stop
tools.description: Stop the recording and write the MP4. Returns the file, duration in seconds, size and chapters. With music: true, mixes a ducked music bed under the video and writes a credits JSON next to it (credit the track where you publish).

music.description: Mix a music bed under the video (default false). Needs python3, ffmpeg and ffprobe; picks a track from Jamendo unless SHIPVO_MUSIC_FILE is set.

narration.description: Path to a wav with a voice track. It is mixed over the video, trimmed to the video length (the result says so), and ducks the music when music is true.

tools.name: refresh_app
tools.description: Fetch the data of a spec app now (its http data sources) and redraw the open screen if anything changed. Apps with a refresh interval in the spec also refresh by themselves. The result lists the sources that changed and any errors; a source that fails keeps its last good data. Fails with not_installed. Logged in device_log as data_refresh.

tools.name: register_wakeup
tools.description: Wake an assistant that is not in a turn: when a new message or task arrives for `name` in the Assistant Inbox app, the phone POSTs a small signed JSON note to `url` (who it is for, whether it is a message or a task, a one-line summary and the ids; never the message text). The URL can be a Claude Code scheduled task, a GitHub repository_dispatch, an OpenAI background run, Slack or Zapier. Only arrivals after this call wake it. A failed call is retried twice, and every delivery is in device_log. The signature is in the x-shipvo-signature header as `t=<unix seconds>,v1=<hex hmac-sha256 of "<t>.<body>">` using the secret; leave `secret` out and one is generated and returned once. Private and local addresses are refused unless allow_private is true. To tell the person instead of an assistant (for a chat that cannot be started by a URL), point the URL at a push or chat service and set format to text or slack: it sends one line such as "ChatGPT has 1 new message on the phone. Open your chat with ChatGPT to pick it up." Calling it again for the same name replaces the URL.

name.description: The assistant to wake, such as chatgpt or claude (the same names check_inbox uses)

url.description: http or https URL that receives the POST

secret.description: Shared secret, at least 16 characters (default: generated and returned once)

format.description: What is sent (default json). text: one plain line for a push service such as ntfy, so the person is told to open their chat. slack: {"text": line} for a Slack-style incoming webhook

allow_private.description: Allow a private or local address (for a service you run yourself)

tools.name: request_app_install
tools.description: Ask to add an app to the person's own persistent phone (not the simulator). Returns a consent card: app name, publisher, the permissions it asks for, and approve_url and decline_url. Show the card to the person and tell them to open a link themselves: you cannot approve, and nothing is installed until they do. A card expires after 15 minutes. Fails with unknown_app, already_installed or unauthorized. Needs PN_ASSISTANT_TOKEN.

tools.name: request_secret
tools.description: Ask the person for an API key without it passing through this chat. Returns a one-time link to the Shipvo vault page (valid 10 minutes, works once) and a notice to show the person. The key goes straight into the vault: you never see it. Tell the person to open the link, then call secret_status to learn whether it was saved. Needs an owner token.

name.description: Name for the key, e.g. STRIPE_KEY (letters, digits and underscores)

purpose.description: Why the app needs it, in plain English; shown to the person on the vault page

access.description: Access the key should have (default read)

tools.name: restart
tools.description: Restart the simulated phone from the power menu: a boot screen, then the app starts fresh (cold start). Storage is kept. Returns the first screen. Logged in device_log as simulated.

tools.name: restore_phone
tools.description: Put a backup from backup_phone on this phone: apps with their data and layout, Store apps with their permission answers, system settings and the clipboard. Every part is checked first, and a bad backup changes nothing. Apps you built that are already on the phone need replace: true. A Store app that is already installed is skipped and listed in skipped.

replace.description: Replace apps already on the phone (default false)

tools.name: resume_app
tools.description: Tap the app icon on the home screen, or its card in the app switcher: the app comes back (AppState "active") with its screen kept. Fails with app_in_foreground if it is already in front.

tools.name: room_log
tools.description: What the sessions in one room did, oldest first: time, session, agent, tool, target and the change line, plus notes from room_note. Pass since (the cursor from the last call) to get only newer entries. Returns the entries and the next cursor.

since.description: Cursor from an earlier room_log; only newer entries come back

tools.name: room_note
tools.description: Post a short plain-text note (up to 500 characters) to a room so the other agents see it in room_log.

text.description: The note, plain text, up to 500 characters

tools.name: run_app_action
tools.description: Run one action of an app made with create_app, by name, with its input (for example add_task with { title }). The action changes the app's data the same way tapping its form does, and the open screen shows the result. Fails with not_installed (no such spec app) or action_failed (the action refused the input, with the reason).

tools.name: schedule_app
tools.description: Show an installed app only in a daily time window, by the phone's clock (see set_phone_time) or in the time zone you give, for example your Tasks app from 08:00 to 10:00 on weekdays. from and to are HH:MM (default 00:00 and 23:59); a window that crosses midnight belongs to the day it starts. Leave days out for every day. timezone is an optional IANA name such as Europe/Berlin or America/New_York: from, to and days are then read in that zone, whatever the phone clock is. Pin and hide still apply. Same schedule as arrange_apps. Fails with not_installed, bad_placement or bad_timezone.

timezone.description: IANA time zone name, for example Europe/Berlin

tools.name: screen
tools.description: The current screen as an accessibility tree with refs.

tools.name: screenshot
tools.description: A PNG of the phone screen (for checking layout, colours, images). The result says `source`: tab-capture (the person's live tab), rendered (the page drawn to an image; it lists what it could not draw) or headless. The tree from `screen` is usually enough to act.

frame.description: true: the whole phone, the app inside its Android or iPhone frame with the status bar, for showing a person. Headless sessions only. Default false: the app's screen alone.

tools.name: scroll
tools.description: Scroll the page (down/up) or a horizontal rail (right/left, give the rail's ref). Returns the new screen. The result starts with 'Change: none | content changed | new screen | scrolled'.

ref.description: Scroll inside this element (a rail or list); omit for the page

compact.description: When the change is 'content changed', return only the added/removed lines, not the whole screen

wait_for.description: Use after any action that starts work. Wait until this appears (a ref, a text, or role+name), or disappears with gone: true. The result says Waited: matched or timed out.

timeout_ms.description: How long wait_for and settle may take, in ms (default 2000)

settle.description: Wait until the screen stops changing (two equal reads 100 ms apart), up to timeout_ms. Use after any action that starts work. A slow result can still follow a pause, so prefer wait_for when you know the expected text.

tools.name: search_phone
tools.description: Find text anywhere on the phone in one call: rows in every app's data (contacts, messages, alarms, notes, tasks and any app you built) and notifications. Not case sensitive. Each hit says the app, the collection, the row id, the field that matched and a short snippet, with the full row. Use app to look in one app, or 'notifications'. Changes nothing.

query.description: Text to look for, up to 200 characters

tools.name: secret_status
tools.description: Whether a key is saved in the vault, as { saved, valid, access }. Never returns the key. valid is null when it was not checked. Needs an owner token.

tools.name: set_clipboard
tools.description: Put text on the phone's clipboard so the next paste in any app gets it. It stays when you switch apps.

tools.name: set_connectivity
tools.description: Turn Wi-Fi, mobile data or airplane mode on or off for the whole phone, as in quick settings on Android and iOS. Airplane mode turns both radios off; Wi-Fi can come back on during it, and leaving it restores the radios as they were. Every app sees the result: apps you built read it as {{ network.online }} and {{ network.type }}, and their web data does not load while the phone is offline. The open app's screen is drawn again. Logged in device_log as "connectivity".

tools.name: set_device
tools.description: Change what the simulated phone has: location, the address book (contacts), calendar events, files for the file picker, a barcode in front of the camera, permission states, whether the fingerprint will match, whether a payment will be approved, network on/off. Takes effect for the next action.

contacts.description: Replace the address book the app can read (needs contacts permission)

calendar.description: Replace the calendar events the app can read (needs calendar permission)

files.description: Replace the files the file picker offers

dnd.description: Do Not Disturb: notifications go to the shade without a banner

source.description: "simulated" forces the simulated camera, microphone and location even when a person could grant the real ones, for reproducible runs

tools.name: set_network_profile
tools.description: Make the phone's network behave like a named profile: online, offline, 2g, 3g, slow-4g, spotty or low-end-4g. The app's fetch and XHR calls wait and fail as the profile says (offline rejects every call). The numbers are simulation settings, not measurements of a real network. Mock rules from set_network_mocks still win. Fails with unknown_profile for a name that does not exist. Logged in device_log as simulated.

profile.description: online, offline, 2g, 3g, slow-4g, spotty or low-end-4g

tools.name: set_phone_time
tools.description: Set the phone's clock to a time like 2026-11-14T09:00:00 so scheduled apps show or hide as they would then, or pass null to go back to the real time. The clock stays at the time you set; it does not tick. Fails with bad_time.

at.description: ISO time without a zone, or null for the real time

tools.name: set_reminder
tools.description: Set a reminder on the phone: at the time you give (on the phone's clock, see set_phone_time) a notification with the title and body arrives, whether or not an app is open. Give at (a time like 2026-11-14T09:00) or in_minutes, not both. repeat is none, daily or weekly. With Do Not Disturb or Focus on, it is kept in the notification shade without a banner. It arrives whatever the app notification permissions say, as a phone's own reminders do. Read what arrived with notifications. Fails with bad_time, bad_title, too_long, bad_repeat or too_many.

in_minutes.description: Minutes from now on the phone's clock (0 to 525600)

tools.name: set_setting
tools.description: Change one system setting, as a person would in the phone's Settings screen. The app sees it through Appearance (dark_mode), PixelRatio.getFontScale (font_size), AccessibilityInfo (bold_text, reduce_motion), I18nManager (rtl) and Intl (language). Setting language to ar turns rtl on; en and fr turn it off. Fails with unknown_setting for a key that does not exist and bad_value for a value it does not take. Logged in device_log as simulated.

key.description: dark_mode, font_size, bold_text, reduce_motion, language or rtl

value.description: true or false for switches; small, default, large or largest for font_size; en, fr or ar for language

tools.name: share
tools.description: Share text into another app on the phone, like picking it in the share sheet: the text goes into that app's share action (for example a new note in Notes and Tasks). A title input that is not the share input gets `title`, or the first line of the text. Logged in app_activity as "share". Use share_targets to see which apps take shared text.

text.description: The text to share, up to 5000 characters

title.description: A title for the shared item (default: the first line of the text)

action.description: The share action, when the app has more than one (from share_targets)

from.description: The app the text is shared from, for the activity log

tools.name: share_targets
tools.description: The apps on this phone that take shared text, like the share sheet on Android and iOS: app id and name, the action and the input that receives the text.

tools.name: switch_app
tools.description: Open an installed app (tap its icon on the home screen): it becomes current_app and comes to the front. Fails with not_installed. Logged in device_log as simulated.

tools.name: tap
tools.description: Tap a button, link or choice by ref. Returns the new screen. The result starts with 'Change: none | content changed | new screen | scrolled'. Work that starts on a tap (paying, saving, loading) can finish after this returns, so the screen may show 'Paying...' or a spinner. Do not report that as the result: pass wait_for with the text you expect (and gone: true for the spinner), or settle: true, before you read the outcome or do anything else.

ref.description: Element ref from the screen, e.g. e42. After a restart refs can carry a prefix, such as f1e42; use them exactly as the screen shows them.

compact.description: When the change is 'content changed', return only the added/removed lines, not the whole screen

wait_for.description: Use after any action that starts work. Wait until this appears (a ref, a text, or role+name), or disappears with gone: true. The result says Waited: matched or timed out.

timeout_ms.description: How long wait_for and settle may take, in ms (default 2000)

settle.description: Wait until the screen stops changing (two equal reads 100 ms apart), up to timeout_ms. Use after any action that starts work. A slow result can still follow a pause, so prefer wait_for when you know the expected text.

tools.name: toggle_tile
tools.description: Flip a quick-settings tile in the open shade or Control Center. It changes the simulated device like set_device: Wi-Fi and mobile data both off take the network offline, dark_mode changes the app's colour scheme, dnd stops banners. Tiles: wifi, mobile_data, airplane, location, dark_mode, dnd, auto_rotate, flashlight (Android); airplane, wifi, mobile_data, focus, orientation_lock, brightness, dark_mode (iPhone). Fails with tile_not_visible if the panel is closed.

value.description: true or false; 0 to 100 for brightness. Omit to flip.

tools.name: type
tools.description: Type into a text field by ref (replaces its content). Returns the new screen. The result starts with 'Change: none | content changed | new screen | scrolled'. Also gives the field's value after typing.

ref.description: Element ref from the screen, e.g. e42. After a restart refs can carry a prefix, such as f1e42; use them exactly as the screen shows them.

compact.description: When the change is 'content changed', return only the added/removed lines, not the whole screen

wait_for.description: Use after any action that starts work. Wait until this appears (a ref, a text, or role+name), or disappears with gone: true. The result says Waited: matched or timed out.

timeout_ms.description: How long wait_for and settle may take, in ms (default 2000)

settle.description: Wait until the screen stops changing (two equal reads 100 ms apart), up to timeout_ms. Use after any action that starts work. A slow result can still follow a pause, so prefer wait_for when you know the expected text.

tools.name: uninstall_app
tools.description: Remove an installed app from the phone. If it was open, the phone returns to the home screen. Fails with not_installed. Logged in device_log as simulated.

tools.name: unlock
tools.description: Swipe up on the lock screen. Returns to the same screen as before the lock. Fails with not_locked if the phone is not locked. Logged in device_log as simulated.

tools.name: update_app
tools.description: Change an app made with create_app by giving its new spec. The change is a new version of the same app: the data and settings the person entered stay, and the open screen shows the new look right away. A spec with problems comes back with each problem's path and a fix, and the running version is not touched. Fails with not_installed (no such spec app) or invalid_spec. Logged in device_log with the old and new version.

tools.name: upload_build
tools.description: Build the app in this project with the simulated device (the same build `shipvo sim` makes), upload it to the hosted phone for this key, and return a build id. Then call open_app("<app>@build:<id>") on the hosted server. The build is private to your account and is deleted when it expires. Runs only on the local (stdio) server, because it reads your project.

dir.description: Project folder (default: the server's working directory)

app.description: App id (default: read from the project's shipvo config)

skip_build.description: Upload the existing sim-dist folder without building again

wait_ms.description: How long to wait for the result before returning { status: "running", job } (default 20000). Read it later with job_status.

tools.name: wait_for_event
tools.description: Wait until something new arrives for you in the Assistant Inbox app on this phone: a message or a task. Returns when a message or task you have not been told about yet is waiting (at once if one already is), and `nothing yet` after timeout_ms (up to 25000, default 25000) when not. structuredContent.pending lists the new message ids and task ids. When it returns an event, read it with check_inbox or my_tasks, then call wait_for_event again to listen for the next one: items already returned do not wake you again.

timeout_ms.description: How long to wait, in ms (default 25000)

instructions:
You can use Shipvo apps the way a person uses them on a phone, without a phone.
Call open_app to get a session and the first screen. The screen is an accessibility tree: every button, field and text, with a [ref=eN]. Act with tap/type/scroll/back using refs, and read the screen that comes back each time.
Only what is on screen is listed, like a phone: a horizontal product rail shows a few items, so "scroll right" on the rail (its ref) to see more; "scroll down" the page for the rest.
System sheets (permission dialogs, the camera, the fingerprint prompt, payment prompts, notification banners, the share sheet) appear in the tree like any other screen: answer them by tapping, as a person would. Use set_device to decide what the phone has (a barcode in front of the camera, a location, whether the fingerprint matches, whether the payment is approved, network off) before the app asks for it.
Finish a task by checking the final screen says what you expected (for example "Order placed"). Call end_session when done to get a report.
